concepts: rotation extrapolation, temporal pattern, shape detection, fixed‐pivot rotation
description: The input is divided into three equal panels laid out left to right, each on a solid black background. In each panel you see the same red semicircular arc (uniform thickness), centered in its panel, rotated clockwise by a constant angle from one panel to the next.   To produce the output, append a fourth panel to the right (same dimensions and black background) and draw the red arc there rotated once more by the same fixed angle around its center pivot—preserving its size, thickness, and color.
visual_elements: red arc (semicircular) shape with uniform thickness
no other objects or colors present
static_patterns: red color and line thickness of the arc stay constant
shape’s size and proportions never vary
central position of the arc does not shift
dynamic_patterns: the red arc rotates smoothly clockwise over time
rotation is continuous (no sudden jumps or pauses)
no scaling, color change, or translation accompanies the rotation
the pivot point of rotation remains fixed at the arc’s center
core_principles: rotational motion about a fixed axis causes the angular displacement of the arc
inertia maintains the shape’s integrity during the rotation
absence of external forces (beyond the pivot constraint) allows a smooth, uniform rotation
Most fundamental principle: the arc undergoes continuous rotation around a fixed central axis.
